report.source_text: The patient was subsequently initiated on B12 supplementation therapy, administered as a 1000 mcg injection once a week for 8 weeks, with subsequent resolution of her lower extremity symptoms, improvement in her gastrointestinal symptoms, and continued normal Vitamin B12 levels and complete blood counts.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 20-year-old woman with T1DM and IgA deficiency presented with nocturnal diarrhea, left lower quadrant pain, nausea, and neuropathy symptoms. Neurological exam confirmed diminished sensation consistent with diabetic neuropathy. Upper endoscopy was grossly unremarkable, but gastric biopsy histology revealed a pattern consistent with autoimmune gastritis. Serum studies showed elevated fasting gastrin and parietal cell antibody levels without macrocytic anemia or vitamin B12 depletion. She was treated with B12 injections, resulting in resolution of neuropathy symptoms and improvement in gastrointestinal symptoms with maintained normal B12 and blood counts.
